faqs.q: What is the average marine biologist salary in Australia?
faqs.a: There is no single published figure for marine biologist salary Australia, but the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult professionals at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352 before tax. Actual pay depends on the applicable award, classification, experience, and employer. For precise rates, check the relevant award via the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary for a marine biologist role?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 gross per year. If you work fewer hours or have unpaid breaks, adjust the weeks accordingly. The calculator on this site does that automatically and also shows your fortnightly take-home pay after tax and Medicare.

faqs.q: Does the marine biologist salary include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, the quoted salary is your ordinary-time earnings before super. Employers must pay super guarantee (12% from 1 July 2025) on top of your ordinary-time earnings for most employees, including casuals. So if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer should also contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost to the employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Marine Biologist Salary Australia: Understanding the Numbers

If you are searching for a **marine biologist salary Australia**, you likely want to know how an hourly rate or a job offer translates into an annual figure, a fortnightly take-home amount, and what you can expect after tax and super. This guide walks you through the conversion using the standard Australian full-time assumption of 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year, and it explains how the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and superannuation fit in.

### The Basic Conversion: Hourly to Annual

The core formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = annual gross salary**. For a full-time employee, the standard hours per week is 38, as set by the Fair Work Act. So if you are offered a marine biologist role at $45 per hour, the annual gross pay is:

$45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920

This is the amount before tax, Medicare, and any salary packaging. It assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. If you work part-time or have unpaid gaps, adjust the hours or weeks accordingly. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site lets you change both.

### Fortnightly Pay and Take-Home

Most Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To get your gross fortnightly amount, multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the $45/hour example:

- Weekly gross: $45 × 38 = $1,710
- Fortnightly gross: $1,710 × 2 = $3,420

After applying the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy (2%), the estimated take-home pay for this example is about $2,690 per fortnight. That figure assumes no HELP debt, no Medicare levy surcharge, and no salary sacrifice. For a detailed breakdown, see the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. However, most marine biologist roles are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. For example, the Health Services Award or the Professional Employees Award may apply depending on the employer and duties. Always check the specific award to ensure you are being paid correctly.

### Casual Loading and Super

If you work as a casual marine biologist, you typically receive a 25% loading on the base rate instead of paid annual leave, personal leave, and notice. That means a casual rate of $50 per hour is roughly equivalent to a permanent rate of $40 per hour before entitlements. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to compare the two.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary-time earnings. From 1 July 2025, the super guarantee is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual salary is $88,920, your employer should contribute an additional $10,670 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost to the employer. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### What the ABS Says About Average Pay

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, which annualises to about $108,352. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118 per year. These figures give a broader context for a **marine biologist salary Australia**, but actual pay depends on your classification, experience, and location.

### Putting It All Together

When evaluating a marine biologist job offer, start with the hourly rate. Multiply by 38 and 52 to get the annual gross. Then subtract estimated tax and Medicare to see your take-home. Remember that super is extra. If you are casual, factor in the 25% loading and compare with permanent roles. Use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page as a baseline, and always verify your award rate through the Fair Work Ombudsman.

This site’s calculator does all the conversions for you, including the fortnightly breakdown and tax estimates. It uses the 2026–27 tax scale and the Medicare levy. The results are estimates only, not a determination of your actual pay or tax liability. For personalised advice, consult a registered tax agent or the Australian Taxation Office.

### Key Takeaways

- **Standard assumption:** 38 hours per week, 52 weeks per year.
- **Formula:** hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross.
- **Fortnightly:** weekly gross × 2.
- **Minimum:** $26.44/hour permanent, $33.05/hour casual (from 1 July 2026).
- **Super:** 12% paid on top, up to $270,830.
- **Tax:** 2026–27 resident rates with full tax-free threshold.

Whether you are a recent graduate or an experienced marine biologist, understanding these numbers helps you negotiate confidently and plan your finances. The Fair Work Ombudsman and the ABS are your best sources for accurate, up-to-date pay information.
